text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A general consensus at the Arab League on freezing relations and suspending multi-lateral negotiations with Israel...the resolutions will be released today. President Hosni Mubarak reviews the latest developments with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and the foreign ministers of Qatar, Bahrain and Lebanon.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri to head meetings of the economic group to discuss the investment projects which will take Egypt to the 21st century.
- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily said there is a plan to increase exports by 10 percent a year for a period of five years. There is a big market for Egyptian exports in Asia and Africa.
- Important recommendations by the Arab foreign ministers. Arab boycott of Israel to continue until there is a complete and just peace.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says: I have informed Mubarak about the decisions of the ministers. U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is disturbed at developments in the region.
- Parliament to pass out attendance roster to stop MPs from skipping sessions. Sessions were delayed because of absentism.
- Mubarak discussed the dangerous situation with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and the Arab foreign ministers.
- Justice ministry is discussing a draft law which says claimants should seek arbitration before going to court.
- Cotton export committments reached a total 190,766 bales (623,041 tonnes) so far. Last week's lot were sold to Italy, the Alexandria Cotton Exporters Association said.
